question: A male patient appears quiet and defensive during his fertility workup. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Reassure him that male infertility is always easily cured with surgery
options.B: Provide a private, non-judgmental environment to discuss his concerns openly
options.C: Refer him immediately to a psychiatrist for severe clinical depression
options.D: Insist that his wife answers all the clinical questions for him

explanation: Creating a safe, supportive space helps lower defenses and encourages the patient to share his emotional burdens. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T20#GNS312_U1_T20_h8)

question: Which tool is specifically used to check a patient's risk of falling?

options.A: Braden Scale
options.B: Morse Fall Scale
options.C: Apgar Scoring System
options.D: Glasgow Coma Scale

explanation: Spot on! The Morse Fall Scale looks at walking ability and history to help us figure out who is most likely to fall. [learn more](GST319_U4_T7#GST319_U4_T7_h6)

question: What are the three main parts of the epidemiological triangle?

options.A: Agent, host, and environment
options.B: Source, spread, and susceptibility
options.C: Bacteria, virus, and fungus
options.D: Vector, transmission, and portal

explanation: You nailed it! The epidemiological triangle consists of the infectious agent, the host who can catch it, and the environment where they meet. [learn more](GST114_U2_T5#GST114_U2_T5_h1)

question: Which harmful traditional practice should nurses actively discourage when teaching mothers about diarrhoea?

options.A: Mixing ORS packets in clean drinking water
options.B: Withholding food and fluids to rest the bowel
options.C: Continuing to breastfeed the infant on demand
options.D: Giving zinc supplements for two full weeks

explanation: Never starve a tummy bug! Stopping food and water only makes malnutrition and dehydration worse. Children with diarrhoea need continued feeding and plenty of fluids to heal. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T57#GNS214_U1_T57_h8)

question: Why is balancing the cash register at the end of a shift so important in a DRF unit?

options.A: To prove that the nurses worked longer hours than scheduled
options.B: To ensure that cash collected matches the volume of drugs dispensed
options.C: To decide which drugs are most popular among patients
options.D: To calculate the monthly salary bonus for the nursing staff

explanation: Daily cash reconciliation keeps things transparent, honest, and ensures every single tablet is accounted for. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T7#GNS215_U3_T7_h6)

question: How does eating plenty of fiber help a patient managing diabetes mellitus?

options.A: By slowing down the absorption of carbohydrates in the gut
options.B: By directly acting as a substitute for pancreatic insulin
options.C: By accelerating the breakdown of simple sugars in the stomach
options.D: By entirely blocking the digestion of dietary fats

explanation: Fiber acts like a speed bump in the digestive tract, slowing down how fast sugar enters the bloodstream and preventing those sudden spikes after a meal. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T008#GNS227_U7_T008_h3)

question: At what age should solid foods be introduced alongside breast milk or formula?

options.A: Twelve months
options.B: Six months
options.C: Three months
options.D: Nine months

explanation: You got it! By six months, breast milk alone isn't quite enough to match a growing baby's big nutritional demands, so it's time for tasty complementary foods. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T12#GNS216_U6_T12_h5)

question: Why do nurses need to speak up and do advocacy work alongside regular bedside care?

options.A: Patients will refuse medications unless nurses also lobby local leaders
options.B: Hospital management requires nurses to submit weekly political reports
options.C: Clinical care alone cannot fix underlying systemic gaps causing illness
options.D: Clinical nursing duties do not take up enough of a nurse's work shift

explanation: Great thinking! Treating patients at the bedside is vital, but if bad living conditions or broken policies keep making people sick, we have to advocate for wider changes too. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T8#GNS124_U4_T8_h1)

question: A massive passenger train crash is classified under which type of disaster?

options.A: Technological Industrial Leaks
options.B: Transportation Disasters
options.C: Biological Contaminations
options.D: Natural Weather Anomalies

explanation: You got it! Accidents involving mass transport like trains, planes, and large buses are grouped as transportation disasters. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T5#GNS315_U1_T5_h2)

question: What is the term for a nurse's legal obligation to answer for their professional actions?

options.A: Professional accountability
options.B: Informed consent
options.C: Beneficence
options.D: Vicarious liability

explanation: Exactly! Accountability means owning up to both the good and bad outcomes of the care you provide. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T12#GNS321_U2_T12_h2)

question: Why is it important to ask a patient about their job and workplace environment during a social history?

options.A: It helps calculate the exact monthly income of the patient
options.B: It determines how many days off work the patient needs
options.C: Certain jobs expose workers to toxins that cause chronic illness
options.D: It shows whether the patient enjoys their daily job duties

explanation: Well reasoned! Workplace exposures like dust, fumes, or heavy lifting often play a big role in lung or body pains. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T1#GNS124_U6_T1_h6)

question: Which part of the pleura has a very rich supply of pain fibers?

options.A: Visceral pleura
options.B: Pulmonary parenchyma
options.C: Parietal pleura
options.D: Mediastinal fat

explanation: Spot on! The parietal pleura lines your chest wall and is packed with pain receptors. That is why procedures in this area can feel quite uncomfortable for the patient. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T12#GNS125_U3_T12_h2)

question: When a doctor prescribes medication for a child's conduct disorder, what is the main purpose?

options.A: Permanently curing the underlying behaviour disorder
options.B: Targeting specific symptoms like severe aggression or hyperactivity
options.C: Replacing the need for any behavioral therapy
options.D: Ensuring the child gets higher grades in school

explanation: Medications are used alongside therapy to control tough, disruptive symptoms—they aren't a standalone cure, but they offer great relief. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T1#GNS314_U2_T1_h6)

question: What is the primary practical purpose of estimating maternal mortality in a country?

options.A: To determine the total population growth rate of newborns
options.B: To punish hospitals that report high numbers of patient deaths
options.C: To allocate healthcare resources and target interventions effectively
options.D: To calculate annual tax deductions for pregnant mothers

explanation: Accurate estimates allow health planners to see where the greatest dangers lie and direct resources and emergency care improvements to those areas. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T016#GNS226_U1_T016_h2)

question: What is the main difference between medical asepsis (clean technique) and surgical asepsis (sterile technique)?

options.A: Surgical asepsis relies entirely on chemical disinfectants rather than physical barriers
options.B: Surgical asepsis eliminates all microorganisms, while medical asepsis reduces their number and spread
options.C: Medical asepsis is used only in operating theatres, while surgical asepsis is for general wards
options.D: Medical asepsis destroys bacterial spores, whereas surgical asepsis only targets viruses

explanation: Well done! Clean technique (medical asepsis) cuts down germ numbers, while sterile technique (surgical asepsis) wipes out every single micro-organism. [learn more](GST114_U2_T5#GST114_U2_T5_h4)

question: In health economics, what does 'supply' actually refer to?

options.A: The total number of patients waiting to be seen in an emergency department
options.B: The quantity of healthcare goods and services providers are willing and able to offer
options.C: The government budget allocated for public health campaigns each year
options.D: The amount of money patients are willing to pay for prescription drugs

explanation: Supply is simply what hospitals, clinics, and health workers make available for people to use—like hospital beds, drugs, and clinic hours. [learn more](GST322_U1_T1#GST322_U1_T1_h4)

question: Which parts of the body usually show the earliest physical signs of a nutrient deficiency?

options.A: Internal organs like the liver, kidneys, and pancreas
options.B: Rapid-turnover tissues like skin, hair, and mucous membranes
options.C: Dense connective tissues like cartilage and deep ligaments
options.D: Structural elements like cortical bone and long bones

explanation: Tissues that grow and shed quickly need a constant supply of nutrients, so they show signs of trouble first when supplies run low. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T5#GNS124_U6_T5_h3)

question: What is another name for the channels that run across compact bone to supply blood?

options.A: Canaliculi
options.B: Volkmann's canals
options.C: Haversian canals
options.D: Lacunae

explanation: Great! Volkmann's canals run across (perpendicular to) the bone shaft, bringing blood vessels from the outside surface into the inner bone structure. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T2#GNS121_U3_T2_h5)

question: As a nurse, what is one of your main roles when it comes to nutrition and diet therapy?

options.A: Translating nutrition therapy into practical everyday habits for patients
options.B: Writing the definitive medical nutrition prescription for the hospital kitchen
options.C: Designing institutional food service menus for surgical wards
options.D: Diagnosing rare nutritional deficiencies using laboratory blood work

explanation: You are the vital link between doctor's orders and real life! Your job is to help patients take clinical nutrition advice and fit it smoothly into their daily meals and lifestyle. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T008#GNS227_U7_T008_h1)

question: How did nursing education in Nigeria change after the country gained independence in 1960?

options.A: Universities began offering degree programs in nursing science
options.B: Training was moved entirely out of hospitals into military camps
options.C: All foreign-trained nurses were banned from practicing locally
options.D: Traditional herbalism completely replaced western pharmacology

explanation: After independence, nursing grew rapidly as a profession, and Nigerian universities started offering degree courses to elevate nurse training. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T2#GNS112_U1_T2_h4)

question: A patient with high cholesterol asks which fat to avoid completely. What should you tell them?

options.A: Trans fats
options.B: Omega-3 fatty acids
options.C: Polyunsaturated oils
options.D: Monounsaturated fats

explanation: Trans fats are artificial troublemakers! They raise bad cholesterol and lower the good kind, so it's best to avoid them for a healthy heart. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T011#GNS227_U4_T011_h2)

question: Why do nurses check vital signs before giving certain medications?

options.A: To fulfill a mandatory paperwork requirement for hospital insurance
options.B: To make sure the patient's current physical status is safe for that specific drug
options.C: To distract the patient from feeling nervous about the injection
options.D: To test if the thermometer and blood pressure cuff are working correctly

explanation: Checking vitals first helps you catch things like low blood pressure or a slow heart rate before giving a drug that could drop them even lower. Safety first! [learn more](GNS125_U4_T5#GNS125_U4_T5_h3)

question: A nurse checks a patient's blood pressure thirty minutes after giving a blood pressure medication to see if it dropped into the normal range. Which phase of the nursing process is this?

options.A: Planning
options.B: Evaluation
options.C: Diagnosis
options.D: Assessment

explanation: Checking the results after an intervention to see if goals were met is the definition of the evaluation phase. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h8)

question: Which part of the nephron reabsorbs the biggest share of filtered bicarbonate?

options.A: Loop of Henle
options.B: Distal convoluted tubule
options.C: Collecting duct
options.D: Proximal convoluted tubule

explanation: You've got this! The proximal convoluted tubule is the hardworking champion that reclaims the vast majority of filtered bicarbonate right back into the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T12#GNS121_U2_T12_h2)

question: Why would a doctor order a pelvic ultrasound for a patient with a suspected incomplete abortion?

options.A: To check the patient's blood group and crossmatch
options.B: To measure hormone levels in the kidneys
options.C: To check for leftover pregnancy tissue in the uterus
options.D: To count the exact white blood cells in the body

explanation: An ultrasound lets the team peek inside the womb to confirm if any pregnancy tissue is still trapped. Super helpful diagnostic tool! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h4)

question: When starting a 'less than' ogive on graph paper, where should your very first point land on the x-axis?

options.A: At the highest possible number recorded in the entire study
options.B: Right in the middle of the very last group listed
options.C: At the exact median value calculated for the sample
options.D: At the lower boundary of the first class where frequency is zero

explanation: That's it! We anchor our 'less than' ogive right at the starting line—the lower boundary of the first class where no data has piled up yet. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T11#GNS217_U4_T11_h4)

question: Why is sharing your computer login password with a colleague during a busy shift dangerous?

options.A: It locks the computer hardware permanently until IT resets it
options.B: It automatically deletes all patient lab reports in the system
options.C: It slows down the hospital internet connection speed significantly
options.D: It breaks accountability because actions under that login are tied to your name

explanation: Every action in an EHR is logged against the active user account, so sharing credentials destroys reliable audit trails. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h4)

question: Why do patients with anaemia often have very pale skin and nail beds?

options.A: There is less red hemoglobin pigment in surface blood vessels
options.B: Blood is completely blocked from reaching the skin surface
options.C: The skin makes extra melanin to protect itself
options.D: Poor circulation causes fluid to collect under the skin

explanation: Hemoglobin is what paints our blood red. When levels drop, that healthy pink color fades from places close to the surface, like the palms, gums, and nail beds. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T6#GNS311_U2_T6_h3)

question: A clinic nurse reads about a brilliant new wound care gadget, but her clinic lacks the budget and steady electricity to run it. What should she consider?

options.A: Whether the study findings fit the practical limitations of her local work environment
options.B: Whether she should resign from her job for not having enough equipment
options.C: Whether the researchers made a math error in their statistical calculations
options.D: Whether all wound care studies should be banned from medical journals

explanation: Local context matters greatly. A great gadget is useless if your clinic doesn't have the resources or steady power to support it! [learn more](GNS224_U2_T3#GNS224_U2_T3_h6)

question: A ward nurse carefully checks expiry dates and avoids opening extra sterile packs during a procedure. What is the nurse showing?

options.A: Risk pooling
options.B: Equity
options.C: Efficiency
options.D: Vertical integration

explanation: Spot on! Preventing waste in the ward is a practical way nurses practice efficiency every single day. [learn more](GST322_U4_T6#GST322_U4_T6_h2)

question: Which structural feature is found in spongy bone instead of compact bone?

options.A: Trabeculae
options.B: Concentric lamellae
options.C: Haversian canals
options.D: Osteons

explanation: Spongy bone is made of a porous network of struts and plates called trabeculae, lacking standard osteon cylinders. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T2#GNS121_U3_T2_h6)

question: What is the best way to communicate with a patient who has a hearing impairment?

options.A: Cover your mouth with a mask to reduce visual distractions
options.B: Face the patient directly and speak clearly at a normal volume
options.C: Shout loudly so the sound waves travel a greater distance
options.D: Speak as quickly as possible to finish the conversation fast

explanation: Facing them lets them catch lip movements and facial cues. Remember: shouting distorts sounds, but speaking clearly at a normal tone works wonders! [learn more](GNS311_U3_T8#GNS311_U3_T8_h4)

question: A hospital completely bans the use of a toxic chemical sterilizing agent and buys a safe machine instead. Which control strategy is this?

options.A: Administrative control
options.B: Work practice change
options.C: Elimination
options.D: Personal protection

explanation: Removing the toxic chemical completely from the facility means the hazard has been eliminated. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T8#GNS225_U7_T8_h3)

question: A nurse checks a patient's blood pressure two hours after giving a BP medication to see if it worked. Which phase of the nursing process is this?

options.A: Evaluation
options.B: Assessment
options.C: Planning
options.D: Diagnosis

explanation: Well done! Checking back to see if your nursing action actually achieved the goal is the exact definition of evaluation. [learn more](GST319_U4_T2#GST319_U4_T2_h3)

question: A patient tests positive for HIV at the clinic. What is your best immediate nursing action?

options.A: Report the patient's name to local community leaders immediately
options.B: Advise the patient to stop working and isolate at home forever
options.C: Provide compassionate post-test counseling and link the patient to treatment services
options.D: Wait until the patient asks questions before saying anything about treatment

explanation: A positive test can be scary. As a nurse, your warmth, privacy, and gentle guidance are vital to connect them straight to the care they need. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T4#GNS214_U1_T4_h5)

question: How does well-integrated health data improve your daily nursing workflow?

options.A: It reduces time spent searching for records and supports proactive care
options.B: It prevents nurses from communicating directly with physicians
options.C: It forces nurses to spend all their shift fixing computer hardware
options.D: It removes all documentation requirements from the nursing shift

explanation: Having all your patient info connected in one place cuts down on annoying delays and helps you catch health problems before they turn into emergencies. You've got this! [learn more](GNS113_U2_T5#GNS113_U2_T5_h7)

question: What is the big advantage of organizing healthcare into different levels (primary, secondary, tertiary)?

options.A: It makes primary health clinics responsible for major surgical operations
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for any communication between nurses and doctors
options.C: It restricts rural clients from ever accessing modern contraceptive methods
options.D: It ensures clients receive care at the appropriate facility matching their medical complexity

explanation: Leveling care makes sure simple things are handled locally, while complex cases go smoothly to places fully equipped for them. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T6#GNS225_U3_T6_h3)

question: Which nail change is most commonly linked to long-term low blood oxygen levels?

options.A: Koilonychia
options.B: Yellowing
options.C: Clubbing
options.D: Paronychia

explanation: You got it! Finger clubbing—where the fingertips broaden and the nail bed softens—happens when the body has dealt with low oxygen for a long time. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T4#GNS112_U5_T4_h3)

question: Which Nigerian government bodies coordinate national and state-level disaster management?

options.A: EFCC and ICPC
options.B: NEPA and PHCN
options.C: JAMB and WAEC
options.D: NEMA and SEMA

explanation: Good to know for your community health postings! NEMA handles things at the national level, while SEMA takes charge at the state level. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T7#GNS315_U1_T7_h9)

question: What does a constructivist view assume about reality in qualitative research?

options.A: Reality is identical for every person with the same illness
options.B: Reality is a fixed physical truth that can be measured
options.C: Reality is subjective and shaped by individual experiences
options.D: Reality is determined strictly by laboratory blood tests

explanation: Spot on! Constructivism teaches that people build their own understanding of reality based on their unique lived experiences and daily interactions. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T5#GNS224_U1_T5_h2)

question: Why should a nurse focus on health problems that residents care about the most?

options.A: It saves the hospital from spending any money on medical supplies
options.B: Residents are more motivated to participate when the project matches their interests
options.C: Government regulations legally force citizens to attend health meetings
options.D: It guarantees that no one in the village will ever fall sick again

explanation: When people see you addressing a problem they actually care about, they will gladly join in and help! [learn more](GNS225_U1_T3#GNS225_U1_T3_h5)

question: How do antibiotics used in agriculture often end up in humans?

options.A: Through the food chain from livestock consumption
options.B: By drinking purified bottled water from wells
options.C: Through direct injection of vaccines in schools
options.D: By airborne dust blowing directly into city hospitals

explanation: When farm animals are given antibiotics, resistant germs can develop in them and pass on to humans through meat handling or consumption. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T18#GNS313_U1_T18_h5)

question: Why is open and honest communication with the patient and family crucial after an adverse event?

options.A: It acknowledges what happened with honesty and helps preserve clinical trust
options.B: It legally transfers all responsibility for recovery to the family members
options.C: It guarantees that no formal incident reports will ever be required
options.D: It prevents the patient from receiving any further medical treatments

explanation: Well done! Being transparent with patients and families builds trust and helps everyone heal emotionally after an unexpected medical mistake. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T6#GNS312_U5_T6_h6)

question: What is usually the very first sign that a patient has taken in too much salt?

options.A: Severe yellow discoloration of the skin and eyes
options.B: Sudden and noticeable weight gain from fluid retention
options.C: Immediate development of a high grade fever
options.D: A sudden drop in resting heart rate below 50 beats per minute

explanation: You got it! Because water chases salt, eating too much sodium quickly shows up on the weighing scale as water weight. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T008#GNS227_U6_T008_h6)

question: What does fertile cervical mucus look and feel like around the time of ovulation?

options.A: Brownish, foul-smelling, and clumpy in texture
options.B: Clear, stretchy, and resembling raw egg whites
options.C: Scant, acidic, and impenetrable to sperm cells
options.D: Thick, sticky, and completely dry to the touch

explanation: High estrogen makes cervical mucus clear and stretchy—just like raw egg white! This special texture helps sperm swim smoothly through the cervix. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T7#GNS121_U5_T7_h5)

question: What is a major nursing priority right after a patient has heart valve surgery for endocarditis?

options.A: Stopping all antibiotic medications once the patient leaves the operating room
options.B: Encouraging immediate heavy physical exercise to strengthen the heart muscle
options.C: Restricting fluid intake completely to prevent any swelling
options.D: Monitoring closely for signs of infection and evaluating neurological status for emboli

explanation: Great nursing care here means staying alert! We watch for any lingering infection and check the patient's brain function (neurological status) to catch any loose clots early. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T6#GNS213_U1_T6_h6)

question: What is the most common cause of death in many inherited neuromuscular disorders?

options.A: Sudden total blindness
options.B: Severe dental decay
options.C: Chronic kidney stones
options.D: Cardiorespiratory failure

explanation: As the muscles controlling breathing and the heart grow weaker over time, it sadly leads to failure in these vital systems. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T16#GNS222_U4_T16_h4)

question: Why should we worry when livestock farmers use antibiotics too frequently?

options.A: It causes animals to stop producing milk entirely
options.B: It can contribute to antimicrobial resistance
options.C: It turns the meat a bright green color
options.D: It makes the meat taste bitter to consumers

explanation: Overusing antibiotics on animals creates tougher, resistant germs that can eventually spread to humans and shrug off our best medications. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T024#GNS227_U2_T024_h3)

question: Which signs and symptoms usually show up first when a person is coming down with Ebola?

options.A: Sudden fever, fatigue, and severe muscle aches
options.B: Profuse internal bleeding and skin bruising
options.C: Paralysis of the lower limbs and blindness
options.D: Productive cough and severe chest congestion

explanation: You nailed it! Early Ebola can easily feel like malaria or typhoid at first—sudden fever and body weakness are the major clues. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T11#GNS214_U1_T11_h3)

question: What is the minimum head-of-bed elevation for a patient on continuous tube feeding?

options.A: 30 to 45 degrees
options.B: 10 to 15 degrees
options.C: Flat on the back
options.D: 60 to 90 degrees

explanation: Spot on! Keeping the head of the bed raised prevents the formula from flowing backward into the lungs. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T001#GNS227_U3_T001_h6)

question: Why are persistent chronic pain medications often prescribed 'by the clock' rather than 'PRN'?

options.A: To reduce the financial cost of purchasing extra tablets
options.B: To maintain a steady blood level and prevent pain from returning
options.C: To make medication administration easier for the night shift nurses
options.D: To ensure the patient takes the maximum possible dose every day

explanation: Giving medications on a scheduled, round-the-clock basis prevents peaks and valleys in drug concentration, keeping constant control over chronic pain. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T14#GNS321_U4_T14_h4)

question: What is the term for the normal, temporary hair shedding that happens after childbirth?

options.A: Androgenetic female baldness
options.B: Alopecia areata universalis
options.C: Hirsutism of the puerperium
options.D: Postpartum telogen effluvium

explanation: Fancy name, simple meaning! 'Telogen effluvium' just describes that normal phase where hair sheds after delivery before the cycle resets. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h4)

question: Why does salivary amylase stop working once food reaches the stomach?

options.A: The stomach absorbs all the leftover saliva immediately
options.B: The food spends too little time in the stomach
options.C: The strong acid in the stomach deactivates the enzyme
options.D: Other enzymes replace it and make it unnecessary

explanation: Salivary amylase loves the neutral mouth environment, but the harsh acid in the stomach shuts it right down. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T11#GNS121_U1_T11_h2)

question: What type of computer is the bedside tablet you use for clinical charting?

options.A: Mainframe
options.B: Microcomputer
options.C: Supercomputer
options.D: Analog processor

explanation: Tablets, laptops, and desktop PCs are all types of microcomputers (or personal computers) built for everyday tasks. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T5#GNS113_U1_T5_h4)

question: What is the clinical term for heartburn?

options.A: Pyrosis
options.B: Peristalsis
options.C: Preeclampsia
options.D: Pruritus

explanation: Pyrosis is simply the medical word for that burning feeling in your chest caused by stomach acid splashing up. You've got this! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T013#GNS226_U2_T013_h1)

question: What is the main job of Langerhans cells in the skin?

options.A: Sensing cold temperatures and gentle touches
options.B: Producing oily sebum to keep the skin soft and waterproof
options.C: Making the dark pigment that shields against sunlight
options.D: Catching and processing foreign invaders for the immune system

explanation: You got it! Langerhans cells are like security guards in the skin—they catch microbes and run to the lymph nodes to sound the alarm. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T3#GNS211_U2_T3_h4)

question: Which of these shows a patient is having trouble with the ADL of 'transferring'?

options.A: The patient forgets to add sugar to their tea.
options.B: The patient cannot balance their monthly bills.
options.C: The patient wears mismatched socks and unbuttoned shirts.
options.D: The patient needs help moving from the bed to a chair.

explanation: Spot on! In nursing, 'transferring' is all about safely moving a patient from one surface to another, like from a bed to a wheelchair. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T5#GNS324_U3_T5_h1)

question: What finding in a pregnant patient's urine points to prolonged vomiting and starvation?

options.A: Ketones
options.B: Red blood cells
options.C: Glucose
options.D: Bilirubin

explanation: When the body can't keep food down, it starts burning its own fat for fuel. This breakdown leaves behind ketones in the urine—a classic sign of prolonged vomiting! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T016#GNS226_U2_T016_h3)

question: Why is passive immunity considered temporary?

options.A: Vaccines prevent passive antibodies from staying in the bloodstream
options.B: The immune system destroys the transferred antibodies immediately
options.C: Maternal antibodies are blocked by the infant's stomach acid
options.D: The body does not manufacture its own memory cells or antibodies

explanation: Passive immunity only supplies ready-made antibodies without teaching the host's cells how to make more, so protection fades away. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T8#GNS313_U1_T8_h4)

question: What is the main difference between infiltration and extravasation?

options.A: Extravasation makes the skin feel very cold, whereas infiltration makes it feel hot
options.B: Infiltration only happens in the legs, while extravasation happens in the arms
options.C: Extravasation involves tissue-damaging vesicant drugs that can cause necrosis
options.D: Infiltration requires immediate surgical removal of the vein tissue

explanation: Both mean fluid leaked out of the vein, but extravasation is extra scary because the leaked drug is a 'vesicant' that can actually destroy the surrounding tissue and cause severe sores. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T17#GNS122_U1_T17_h6)

question: What is the most important factor an educator must check before selecting a teaching aid?

options.A: Whether it has bright, attractive colors
options.B: Whether it matches the lesson objectives
options.C: If it is the most expensive brand available
options.D: If it requires electricity to function

explanation: No matter how advanced a material is, it fails its educational purpose if it does not help achieve the specific learning goals of the class. [learn more](GST321_U8_T4#GST321_U8_T4_h4)

question: A ward has very sick patients and several junior nurses on duty. What is the best staffing approach?

options.A: Pair junior nurses with experienced senior nurses
options.B: Send all the junior nurses home to rest
options.C: Ignore the patient acuity levels when scheduling
options.D: Assign all critical patients to the most junior nurse

explanation: You got it! Teaming up junior nurses with experienced seniors keeps patients safe and helps the junior staff learn safely. [learn more](GST321_U6_T2#GST321_U6_T2_h4)

question: What is a common problem with social welfare systems for people with disabilities in resource-limited settings?

options.A: Bureaucracy is fast and fully digital
options.B: Government healthcare is entirely free and comprehensive
options.C: Benefits are often sporadic, underfunded, and hard to access
options.D: Every citizen gets a guaranteed lifelong pension

explanation: Good policies might exist on paper, but in reality, government support systems are often too weak or irregular to rely on. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T12#GNS225_U5_T12_h5)

question: You want to find out which months malaria cases peak and food is scarcest in a farming village. Which tool should you use?

options.A: A biometric blood test
options.B: A structural house blueprint
options.C: A hospital budget ledger
options.D: A seasonal calendar

explanation: Spot on! Seasonal calendars let you visually map out changes across the year, tracking things like disease cycles and food supply. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T7#GNS124_U3_T7_h4)

question: What is the main job of an analgesic drug?

options.A: To relieve pain without causing unconsciousness
options.B: To reduce high body temperature quickly
options.C: To put the patient into a deep sleep
options.D: To lower elevated blood pressure readings

explanation: Analgesics are medicines that chase away pain while keeping your patient awake and alert so you can still talk to them! [learn more](GNS223_U5_T2#GNS223_U5_T2_h1)

question: Why does calling domestic abuse a 'private family matter' cause harm to victims?

options.A: They discourage outside help and silence victims out of fear
options.B: They guarantee that police officers will investigate immediately
options.C: They provide free legal counseling for all affected families
options.D: They ensure total financial independence for the abused person

explanation: Spot on! Brushing off abuse as a 'family secret' forces victims to suffer alone in the dark, cutting them off from the help and rescue they deserve. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T10#GNS312_U4_T10_h6)

question: Why must nurses in local community clinics look beyond hospital walls when caring for patients?

options.A: Environmental and economic living conditions heavily impact health outcomes
options.B: Nurses are forbidden from providing care outside of enclosed rooms
options.C: Community members never visit hospitals for severe medical problems
options.D: Lab tests can only be accurately performed in outdoor market stalls

explanation: Understanding a patient's home and community environment helps explain why illnesses occur and how to prevent them. [learn more](GNS123_U1_T5#GNS123_U1_T5_h6)

question: What is a tricky downside of pie charts when values are very close to each other?

options.A: Statistical software blocks their creation
options.B: They require complex mathematical formulas to read
options.C: They cannot display percentages greater than 50
options.D: The human eye struggles to compare slice sizes accurately

explanation: Correct! It's genuinely hard for our eyes to tell the difference between two slices that look almost the same size. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T8#GNS217_U4_T8_h5)

question: A nurse manager creates a strict handwashing policy to prevent infections, relying on standard operating procedures. Which theory is primarily applied here?

options.A: Bureaucratic management theory
options.B: Human relations management theory
options.C: Pure contingency management
options.D: Quantitative management science

explanation: Establishing formal rules, standard operating procedures, and safety regulations reflects bureaucratic theory. [learn more](GST321_U1_T3#GST321_U1_T3_h6)

question: Why do pregnant women and young children get severe malaria so easily in Nigeria?

options.A: Their immune defenses are either developing or temporarily lowered
options.B: They have a naturally higher body temperature that attracts vectors
options.C: They spend more time outdoors during peak sunlight hours
options.D: Their diets lack the specific nutrients required to fight protozoa

explanation: You got it! Little ones are still building their immune defenses, and pregnancy naturally lowers a woman's immune response for a bit, making them extra vulnerable. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T3#GNS214_U1_T3_h1)

question: Which sign strongly points to severe pre-eclampsia in a pregnant mum?

options.A: Painful urination and cloudy urine output
options.B: Itchy skin on the palms and soles of the feet
options.C: Frequent hunger and increased thirst
options.D: Sudden severe headache and high blood pressure

explanation: High BP combined with a terrible headache or vision changes is a classic red flag for severe pre-eclampsia. Keep your eyes peeled for this! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T12#GNS225_U3_T12_h2)

question: Which organ handles oxygen and waste exchange for the baby before birth?

options.A: The placenta
options.B: The fetal kidneys
options.C: The fetal liver
options.D: The amniotic sac

explanation: Before birth, the placenta acts as the baby's lungs and kidneys, bringing in oxygen and clearing waste through the umbilical cord. You've got this! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T010#GNS226_U3_T010_h1)

question: What is a major preventive benefit of routine antenatal care (ANC) visits?

options.A: Treating chronic childhood asthma attacks
options.B: Performing immediate emergency cesarean sections
options.C: Providing permanent surgical contraception
options.D: Giving tetanus toxoid vaccines and iron supplements

explanation: Spot on! ANC visits are crucial for delivering preventive care like immunizations and nutritional supplements to protect both mother and baby. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T004#GNS226_U1_T004_h3)

question: Which heart chamber receives oxygenated blood directly from the pulmonary veins?

options.A: Left ventricle
options.B: Left atrium
options.C: Right ventricle
options.D: Right atrium

explanation: The pulmonary veins bring oxygenated blood back from the lungs and empty it straight into the left atrium of the heart. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T9#GNS111_U2_T9_h5)

question: Which part of the brain is the main control center for keeping a person awake and alert?

options.A: Basal ganglia
options.B: Cerebellum
options.C: Reticular activating system
options.D: Medulla oblongata

explanation: Great job! The reticular activating system in the brainstem acts like the brain's alarm clock, controlling wakefulness and your sleep-wake cycle. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T5#GNS221_U3_T5_h1)

question: Which of these is an example of a biological workplace hazard?

options.A: Loud machinery noise
options.B: Repetitive typing motion
options.C: Toxic cleaning solvents
options.D: Hepatitis B virus

explanation: Biological hazards come from living things like germs, bacteria, and viruses (such as Hepatitis B) that can affect healthcare workers and others. You're doing great! [learn more](GNS225_U7_T4#GNS225_U7_T4_h2)

question: A snakebite patient starts bleeding spontaneously and has abnormal clotting lab results. Which toxin is likely at work?

options.A: Myotoxins
options.B: Hemotoxins
options.C: Neurotoxins
options.D: Cytotoxins

explanation: Think 'hemo' for blood! Hemotoxins mess with the body's clotting system, causing bleeding and messy lab results. [learn more](GNS112_U7_T6#GNS112_U7_T6_h2)

question: Why must you wait for the alcohol on the skin to dry before sticking the patient?

options.A: To activate the antiseptic properties of the alcohol
options.B: To ensure the skin surface becomes completely sterile
options.C: To make the outer skin layers easier to pierce
options.D: To prevent stinging and burning sensations upon entry

explanation: Patience pays off! If the alcohol isn't dry, the needle drags it down into the tissue, causing a sharp, unnecessary sting for your patient. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T7#GNS125_U3_T7_h5)

question: What is the main reason to encourage plenty of fluids for a patient with metabolic joint disease?

options.A: To dilute the blood so that red blood cells multiply faster
options.B: To prevent the stomach from absorbing purines from digested food
options.C: To keep the skin moist and prevent breakdown around the joints
options.D: To help the kidneys flush out excess metabolic waste products and prevent crystal formation

explanation: Drinking plenty of water helps the kidneys wash out uric acid before it has a chance to form painful crystals in the joints. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T15#GNS222_U1_T15_h8)

question: A patient with a tummy bug is passing watery stool. Which body system is acting as the portal of exit?

options.A: Cardiovascular system
options.B: Gastrointestinal tract
options.C: Integumentary system
options.D: Respiratory tract

explanation: Spot on! Stool and digestive issues come from the GI tract, making it the exit route for tummy bugs. [learn more](GST114_U2_T2#GST114_U2_T2_h4)

question: What is the single most effective way to stop the spread of infections in the hospital?

options.A: Taking daily antibiotics
options.B: Wearing sterile gloves
options.C: Using room air filters
options.D: Proper hand hygiene

explanation: Simple yet powerful! Washing or sanitizing your hands properly is your number one shield against carrying germs from patient to patient. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T2#GNS122_U2_T2_h4)

question: Why is emotional and psychological support so important for patients dealing with amenorrhoea?

options.A: Emotional support replaces the need for any complex diagnostic blood testing
options.B: Patients will refuse all physical examinations unless their anxiety is treated first
options.C: Psychological stress is the only scientifically proven cause of primary amenorrhoea
options.D: Changes in menstrual patterns often create strong emotional distress regarding identity and fertility

explanation: Not seeing a regular period can be really scary for a young woman, often triggering worries about her womanhood and future family. [learn more](GNS216_U2_T4#GNS216_U2_T4_h8)

question: How is an idiosyncratic drug reaction different from a regular side effect?

options.A: It only happens when a patient takes an overdose of medicine.
options.B: It can be easily predicted by checking standard blood test results.
options.C: It is a mild response that always goes away without any treatment.
options.D: It is completely unpredictable and does not depend on the drug dose.

explanation: Think of an idiosyncratic reaction as a surprise response! Unlike normal side effects that we expect, these happen out of nowhere due to a patient's unique body makeup, not because of a high dose. You've got this! [learn more](GNS125_U5_T9#GNS125_U5_T9_h1)

question: Which personal household item should a patient with Hepatitis B be advised NOT to share with family members?

options.A: Razors and toothbrushes
options.B: Cotton bed sheets
options.C: Glass drinking cups
options.D: Ceramic dinner plates

explanation: Spot on! Razors and toothbrushes can easily trap tiny, microscopic drops of blood, which could accidentally pass the virus to someone else in the house. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T16#GNS313_U2_T16_h7)

question: Why do patients with skin problems easily get secondary bacterial infections?

options.A: They produce an excess amount of oils
options.B: Their immune systems are permanently shut down
options.C: Topical medications attract environmental toxins
options.D: Broken skin allows bacteria to enter deeper tissues

explanation: Spot on! When the skin has cracks or sores, the body loses its first line of defense, making it easy for bacteria to sneak in. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T11#GNS213_U5_T11_h1)

question: Why is the powerful drug Amphotericin B kept strictly for severe, life-threatening fungal infections?

options.A: It is completely ineffective against superficial mucosal yeast infections
options.B: It must be mixed with specific dietary fats to work properly in the body
options.C: It causes severe allergic reactions in every patient who takes it
options.D: It carries a significant risk of serious organ toxicity, especially to the kidneys

explanation: Amphotericin B is famously strong ("Ampho-terrible" to the kidneys!), so doctors only use it when things are really serious. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T3#GNS223_U8_T3_h3)

question: Why are social programs like senior centers so helpful for older adults?

options.A: They provide free prescription drugs for chronic illnesses
options.B: They offer round-the-clock intensive nursing care
options.C: They replace the need for regular medical checkups
options.D: They reduce isolation and promote mental well-being

explanation: Getting together for social activities helps seniors make friends, stay happy, and chase away loneliness. [learn more](GNS321_U3_T7#GNS321_U3_T7_h7)

question: Why is local health research important for nurses in Nigeria?

options.A: Foreign textbooks are too expensive for local nursing students to buy
options.B: International organizations pay large grants exclusively to clinical nurses
options.C: Nigerian hospitals require every nurse to publish a paper before promotion
options.D: Western guidelines do not address specific local health challenges and cultural realities

explanation: You've got this! Local research matters because health issues like malaria management and maternal care need solutions tailored to our environment, rather than just copying foreign data. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h1)

question: What is the best first step for a nurse leader when staff are fighting or disagreeing?

options.A: Ignoring the disagreement until staff resolve it independently
options.B: Reassigning both staff members to opposite shifts immediately
options.C: Addressing the issue promptly through collaborative problem-solving
options.D: Issuing a formal disciplinary warning to all parties involved

explanation: Tackling conflicts early with open talk helps find the root cause before a small misunderstanding ruins teamwork on the ward. [learn more](GST321_U1_T14#GST321_U1_T14_h6)

question: Why do researchers use the exact same questions and words for everyone taking a survey?

options.A: It prevents participants from feeling confused by long medical terms
options.B: It guarantees that every participant will finish the survey faster
options.C: It allows the nurse researcher to change the topic mid-interview
options.D: It ensures all answers can be fairly compared across the group

explanation: Using identical wording means any differences in the responses are due to actual differences between people, not because a question was asked differently. Keep pushing forward! [learn more](GNS224_U1_T22#GNS224_U1_T22_h1)

question: What is the main goal of primary prevention?

options.A: To rehabilitate a patient who suffered a stroke or paralysis
options.B: To cure a chronic illness that has lasted for many years
options.C: To prevent a disease from ever occurring in a healthy person
options.D: To screen a community for early signs of high blood sugar

explanation: You nailed it! Primary prevention is all about stopping health problems before they even start by promoting healthy habits and tackling risk factors. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T1#GNS313_U3_T1_h3)

question: Which color of waste bin is standard for infectious medical waste like sharps in Nigeria?

options.A: Yellow
options.B: Black
options.C: Green
options.D: Brown

explanation: Yellow is the universal and local color code for biohazardous and infectious medical waste. You'll see this everywhere in the wards! [learn more](GST114_U2_T8#GST114_U2_T8_h8)

question: What is a major problem when clinics are not youth-friendly?

options.A: High rates of untreated sexually transmitted infections among teens
options.B: Mandatory health insurance for all teenagers
options.C: Decreased interest in secondary school education
options.D: An immediate surplus of qualified midwives

explanation: If young people feel judged or scared when visiting a clinic, they simply stay away. This means infections and health issues go untreated. Making our clinics welcoming changes everything! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T4#GNS216_U1_T4_h5)

question: How do blood vessel (vascular) diseases lead to erectile dysfunction?

options.A: By causing excessive testosterone production in the testes
options.B: By blocking the normal production of seminal fluid
options.C: By destroying the nerves of the cremasteric muscle
options.D: By impairing adequate blood flow into the cavernous tissues

explanation: You got it! An erection needs good, healthy blood flow to fill the tissues. If vascular disease gets in the way, that flow is restricted. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T11#GNS311_U1_T11_h6)

question: What is the first thing a nurse should do when a worker gets a deep cut at work?

options.A: Ask the worker to fill out an insurance claim form first
options.B: Provide immediate first aid and stabilize the worker
options.C: Wait for the company director to arrive and give permission
options.D: Send the worker home without examining the wound

explanation: Always remember your nursing ABCs and emergency priorities—patient safety and immediate first aid come before any paperwork! [learn more](GNS225_U7_T2#GNS225_U7_T2_h6)

question: Which of the following is NOT a way to prepare for or prevent a disaster?

options.A: Ignoring safety regulations in industrial factories to save money
options.B: Stockpiling emergency medical supplies and personal protective gear
options.C: Conducting routine workplace evacuation drills with employees
options.D: Establishing strong communication links between local emergency agencies

explanation: Easy choice! Disregarding safety codes invites disaster rather than preparing for it. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T5#GNS315_U1_T5_h8)

question: If an unresponsive patient is taking slow, gasping, irregular breaths, how should a nurse respond?

options.A: As an indication to wait for natural breathing to stabilize
options.B: As a sign that the patient is recovering normal oxygen levels
options.C: As agonal respirations requiring immediate start of CPR
options.D: As proof that the airway is clear and no further action is needed

explanation: Don't let those gasps fool you! Agonal gasps are just a reflex when the heart stops. Treat them as cardiac arrest and start CPR right away. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T7#GNS315_U3_T7_h3)

question: Why do we always push iron and folate supplements during antenatal care?

options.A: To cure existing chronic infections in the uterus
options.B: To increase the total body weight of the mother
options.C: To speed up the physical growth of the mother's hair
options.D: To prevent anemia and neural tube defects in the baby

explanation: Iron keeps the mother's blood strong and fights off tiredness (anemia), while folate protects the baby's developing brain and spine. It's a powerful combo! [learn more](GNS324_U3_T14#GNS324_U3_T14_h2)

question: A patient gets amoxicillin plus clavulanic acid for a tough infection. What does clavulanic acid do?

options.A: It acts as a mild sedative to help the patient rest
options.B: It increases urine production to flush out bacterial toxins
options.C: It blocks bacterial enzymes that normally destroy amoxicillin
options.D: It numbs local pain at the site of the infected tissue

explanation: Clavulanic acid is a trusty shield! It stops stubborn bacteria from producing enzymes that would normally chew up and destroy amoxicillin. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T6#GNS125_U5_T6_h4)

question: A patient is physically stable after recovering from an intentional overdose. What is the most important next step in their care?

options.A: Discharge the patient immediately with a warning never to return
options.B: Scold the patient for wasting hospital resources and staff time
options.C: Arrange for a mental health evaluation and ongoing psychological support
options.D: Assume the underlying issue is resolved and stop all observation

explanation: Physical healing is only half the battle. For intentional self-harm, a psychiatric assessment and emotional support before discharge are essential for keeping the patient safe. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T7#GNS215_U5_T7_h7)

question: Which of these measurements is a standard part of checking a patient's nutrition using body measurements (anthropometry)?

options.A: Blood pressure and pulse rate
options.B: Serum electrolyte blood levels
options.C: Cerebrospinal fluid pressure
options.D: Body mass index and height

explanation: Correct! Anthropometry simply means measuring the physical body—height, weight, and BMI are the most common ways we do this in the clinic. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T003#GNS227_U1_T003_h6)

question: Which embryonic tissue helps form your vertebrae and ribs as you develop?

options.A: Endodermal gut lining
options.B: Vascular endothelial cells
options.C: Surface ectoderm layer
options.D: Sclerotome cells from somites

explanation: You've got this! Somites divide into parts, and the sclerotome cells are the ones that migrate around the notochord to build the backbone and ribs. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T1#GNS121_U3_T1_h1)

question: Why do nurses look at time, place, and person (descriptive epidemiology) during an outbreak?

options.A: It punishes health workers who failed to report early cases
options.B: It replaces the need for laboratory blood and stool testing
options.C: It helps form clues about who is getting sick and where the source might be
options.D: It guarantees that no new patients will contract the disease tomorrow

explanation: Spotting patterns in who is falling sick, where, and when helps us hunt down where the disease came from and how to stop it. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T10#GNS313_U1_T10_h3)

question: Which of these is a classic example of indirect contact transmission?

options.A: A nurse catches scabies after handling a patient without gloves
options.B: A farmer develops a hookworm infection walking barefoot in soil
options.C: A baby gets pinkeye (conjunctivitis) from touching a contaminated toy
options.D: A student inhales droplet nuclei from a classmate coughing

explanation: Spot on! Indirect contact happens when you pick up germs from an object (like a toy) rather than touching an infected person directly. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T97#GNS214_U1_T97_h1)

question: Why are newborn babies born with soft spots and flexible skull bones?

options.A: To allow the skull bones to overlap during birth and accommodate rapid brain growth
options.B: To let the cerebrospinal fluid drain easily through the scalp tissues
options.C: To prevent the brain from expanding too quickly before walking begins
options.D: To keep the infant's head cool during high fevers in the first year

explanation: Spot on! That flexibility helps the baby's head squeeze safely through the birth canal and gives the brain plenty of room to grow fast afterwards. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T12#GNS121_U6_T12_h1)

question: What was a major negative consequence when asylums closed too quickly?

options.A: Many vulnerable patients became homeless or ended up in prison
options.B: Mental illnesses disappeared completely from society
options.C: Families refused to ever speak to psychiatric nurses again
options.D: Pharmaceutical companies stopped making all psychiatric drugs

explanation: Because local community clinics lacked proper funding, many discharged patients fell through the cracks of society. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T3#GNS314_U1_T3_h6)

question: What is the main goal of a receptor antagonist antidote?

options.A: To coat the intestinal lining and prevent food digestion
options.B: To occupy the same receptor sites and block the toxin from attaching
options.C: To destroy the toxin molecule directly inside the stomach
options.D: To stimulate the liver to store extra glucose for energy

explanation: An antagonist gets to the parking spot (receptor) first and refuses to leave, blocking the toxin from parking there and causing trouble! [learn more](GNS215_U5_T7#GNS215_U5_T7_h2)

question: What was the traditional view of a man's primary role in family health?

options.A: Clinic scheduler
options.B: Primary caregiver
options.C: Financial provider
options.D: Health educator

explanation: Traditionally, men were viewed mainly as providers of money rather than active participants in daily health care and clinic visits. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h1)

question: Why is it important to involve bedside nurses when drafting clinical standards?

options.A: They perform the actual care and understand practical floor realities
options.B: It guarantees that hospital funding will increase
options.C: It removes the need for any supervisory oversight
options.D: They are the only ones allowed to sign administrative policies

explanation: Frontline nurses know what works in daily practice, making their input vital for creating realistic and usable standards. [learn more](GST321_U1_T20#GST321_U1_T20_h4)

question: What is the primary purpose of a community health nursing care plan?

options.A: To replace all medical textbooks used in nursing schools
options.B: To punish community members who break environmental laws
options.C: To guide practical nursing actions and measure health outcomes
options.D: To serve as a decoration for the office wall of the clinic head

explanation: A care plan is your step-by-step roadmap. It tells you what actions to take, who is responsible, and how to check if things are getting better. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T16#GNS225_U2_T16_h8)

question: Which of these is NOT a good lifestyle change for managing high blood pressure?

options.A: Engaging in regular aerobic exercise
options.B: Increasing dietary sodium intake
options.C: Stopping tobacco smoking completely
options.D: Limiting heavy alcohol consumption

explanation: More salt (sodium) holds onto water in the body and pushes blood pressure up—definitely something we want patients to cut back on! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T14#GNS214_U1_T14_h5)

question: What regulatory body guides the professional practice and scope of nurses in Nigeria?

options.A: Pharmacists Council of Nigeria
options.B: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria
options.C: Federal Ministry of Health
options.D: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria

explanation: The Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria sets the legal boundaries and professional standards for all nursing practice in the country. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T2#GNS125_U3_T2_h1)

question: A male patient comes to the clinic with a thick yellow discharge from his urethra and burning pain when urinating. What is the most likely culprit?

options.A: Benign prostatic hyperplasia
options.B: Acute kidney injury
options.C: Gonococcal urethritis
options.D: Urinary tract bladder stone

explanation: That classic yellow discharge combined with burning urination is a textbook sign of Gonorrhea affecting the urethra. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T1#GNS216_U5_T1_h4)

question: Why is setting up a large IV line so important for an anaemic woman in labor?

options.A: To give oral drugs straight into her veins
options.B: To keep track of her internal body temperature
options.C: To quickly give blood or IV fluids if heavy bleeding starts
options.D: To stop gestational diabetes

explanation: A good, wide cannula is a lifesaver—it lets you pump in blood or fluids instantly if postpartum bleeding happens. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T009#GNS226_U4_T009_h7)

question: What should a QA committee do if there is a sudden increase in surgical wound infections?

options.A: Close the entire hospital permanently
options.B: Blame the patients for having weak immune systems
options.C: Ignore the data because infections are normal after surgery
options.D: Investigate sterilization practices and surgical routines right away

explanation: You got it! A sudden jump in infections is a red flag that requires an immediate check of theatre and ward cleanliness. [learn more](GST319_U4_T4#GST319_U4_T4_h4)

question: A 14-year-old girl is brought to the clinic with chronic anxiety, low self-esteem, and frequent physical complaints with no clear organic cause. What background factor should the nurse suspect?

options.A: Standard adolescent adjustment issues to high school
options.B: Trauma and isolation from an early forced marriage
options.C: Immediate physical recovery from a sports injury
options.D: Mild seasonal affective disorder

explanation: Young brides experience intense psychological pressure, social isolation, and loss of control, manifesting as chronic anxiety and somatic complaints. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T14#GNS312_U1_T14_h3)

question: What is the main reason why many pregnant women experience constipation?

options.A: Drinking water causes the bowels to become blocked
options.B: Prenatal vitamins stop the liver from producing bile
options.C: High levels of progesterone slow down movement through the digestive tract
options.D: The baby takes up all the space in the stomach and intestines

explanation: Pregnancy hormones relax the body's muscles, including the gut. This means digestion slows down a bit, which is totally normal! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T012#GNS227_U2_T012_h5)

question: What is the main goal of using the TNM staging system for lung cancer?

options.A: To determine the extent of disease spread and plan appropriate treatment
options.B: To measure the exact volume of air the lungs can hold
options.C: To calculate the patient's exact daily calorie requirements
options.D: To identify which specific type of cigarette the patient smoked

explanation: Brilliant! TNM helps the team figure out how big the tumor is, if it has reached lymph nodes, and how far it has spread, guiding the best treatment plan. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T11#GNS313_U3_T11_h4)

question: Why must you always lower a hospital bed to its lowest position after finishing a bed change?

options.A: To comply with fire safety codes for emergency exits
options.B: To reduce the risk of injury if the patient tries to get out of bed
options.C: To allow the mechanical bed motor to cool down
options.D: To make it easier for the cleaning crew to mop underneath

question: What is the primary purpose of data organization in nursing research?

question: What type of language should a nurse use when writing home care notes?

question: Why is a vague phrase like 'improving community health' not ideal as a project indicator?

question: Why do water-soluble vitamins dissolve easily in our blood?

question: Which recovery phase involves deep emotional pain and heavy thoughts about quitting nursing altogether?

question: Which study type compares patients who have a specific illness with those who don't, checking to see what they were exposed to in the past?

question: What is the main goal of a medical evacuation (medevac)?

question: What is the primary purpose of communication in community health nursing?

question: What is a fixed cost in a health care facility?

question: What is a key piece of advice to give a patient who just received praziquantel treatment?

question: Which gland gets the message from GnRH and then releases LH and FSH into the bloodstream?

question: A woman is pushing very fast with a large baby facing upward and backward. What is she most at risk for?

question: Why do many victims find it so hard to leave an abusive relationship?

question: What are the finger-like projections of the fallopian tube that catch the released egg called?

question: For a patient with a tough lung infection and thick, trapped pus that won't drain, what type of drug will the doctor likely give intrapleurally?

question: What is the main goal of hygiene care for older school-age children compared to babies?

question: What is the primary risk of poor bladder management in an immobile patient?

question: Why are transparent procurement rules so important in public health?

question: A woman in labor in a remote village has a uterine rupture, but the family cannot find a vehicle to take her to the hospital. Which delay does this represent?

question: In what position should the nurse place the body before rigor mortis sets in?

question: Why is the small pit known as the foramen caecum so special in early human development?

question: What is the absolute golden rule of diet therapy for a patient diagnosed with celiac disease?

question: Which process completely destroys ALL microbial life, including tough spores?

question: Which group is a primary target for specialized nutritional support programs?

question: Which situation best demonstrates a violation of a client's basic healthcare rights?

question: An outsourced cleaning company constantly fails to clean the wards on time. What should hospital management do?

question: What is a major risk if a woman hyperventilates too severely during the second stage of labour?

question: What happens when one system, like local transport, breaks down in a community?

question: A clinic has enough money for either a new blood-pressure machine or routine infant vaccines. As a public health nurse, what should you prioritize?

options.A: Save the money in a personal bank account until next year
options.B: The routine infant vaccines to prevent infectious disease outbreaks
options.C: Split the money evenly to buy broken office furniture
options.D: The blood pressure machine because adult patients complain more

question: What is a key part of holistic nursing care for survivors of harmful traditional practices?

options.A: Focusing strictly on surgical interventions while ignoring emotional needs
options.B: Prescribing strong sedative medications to keep the patient quiet
options.C: Encouraging the patient to cut off all ties with her local community
options.D: Combining physical wound treatment with psychological counseling and social support

question: How can a nurse researcher best cut down on sampling bias?

question: Why do nurses check kidney function (like serum creatinine) before starting certain first-line ARVs?

options.B: It proves whether the patient has active tuberculosis infection

question: Which of these is a good example of objective documentation during a reproductive assessment?

options.C: Patient is probably hiding symptoms due to personal embarrassment
options.D: External genitalia look completely normal and healthy overall

question: What does the popular 20-20-20 rule for eye health involve?

options.D: Looking at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds every 20 minutes

question: Which environmental hazard should be removed from a room to protect a patient with a mobility impairment?

options.A: Heavy wooden wardrobes
options.B: Overhead ceiling lights
options.C: Loose throw rugs
options.D: Wall-mounted handrails

question: In infection control, what do we call a 'reservoir'?

options.C: A place where pathogens live and multiply
options.D: The physical barrier used to block germs

question: Why is twisting your body while lifting a heavy patient a big risk?

options.D: It causes the nurse to drop the patient's legs

question: The vaccine refrigerator temperature is rising and the motor is completely silent. What is the very first thing the nurse should check?

question: Why do bedridden patients often need extra protein in their diet?

options.A: Bed rest causes the body to sweat out all available amino acids

options.C: Illness and immobility trigger a state that breaks down muscle
options.D: Proteins are needed to lubricate the moving joints directly

question: What is the best approach when advising a pregnant mum on a tight budget about her diet?
